findings.text: The Homeric song gives Hephaestus's craft a sequence whose ending changes its meaning. Helios observes and informs. Hephaestus forges bonds whose fineness hides their operation. The lovers are caught, the gods are summoned and the scene becomes a public display. The demands for returned bride-gifts and an adulterer's fine introduce distinct accounts. Hermes's willingness to accept even more bonds for the desired encounter shows that exposure does not produce one shared valuation; the goddesses' withdrawal and the gods' laughter have different positions within the spectacle. [Homer, selected sequence](../../../sources/classical-philology/homer/homer-1919-odyssey-murray/SOURCE.md#passages).
findings.reason: All named source actors retain different receptions: Heliosdetection, hiddenbonds, capture/publicdisplay, separatebridegift/fine accounts, Hermesvaluingdesiredencounter, goddesseswithdrawal and godslaughter. Publicexposure does not produce one sharedvaluation; the whole continuation separately develops contingentundertaking/release. Not a generic defensive negation.

findings.text: The avatar brings a wider presence into a particular encounter. In this authored use, descent names the movement into a form that can act: a voice rather than every possible voice, a gesture rather than intention without expression, an entrusted representative rather than an undertaking with no bearer. The presence is not made unreal by having an appearance. It acquires an occasion on which it can matter.
findings.reason: Actual authoreddescent gives presence an operativeparticularform/voice/gesture/entrustedbearer. Appearance does not make that relation unreal; this is positive source-form ontology rather than a historicalavatar doctrine or extra implementation result.

findings.text: Regard returns through the form to the participant who can answer it. The answer need not confirm the first question. It can disclose an omitted circumstance, refuse an imposed role, correct an attributed statement or show that the criterion itself has misnamed the encounter. The result is another determination with a changed history. Maintained personhood does not require an essence displayed without mediation; it requires that continuity of address not become ownership of the person addressed.
findings.reason: Participant’s reply can disclose omittedcircumstance/refuse imposedrole/correctattribution/criterionfault; continuityofaddress doesnotpossess theperson. A fullyunmediated essence is not required for real personhood. Bothsourceanswerability and fittingcriterion retention remain possible.

findings.text: The puzzle travels into the world it claims to depict. Its maker encounters a turn which the flat arrangement cannot preserve, a continuation beyond an edge, a view whose apparent distortion changes with position. The image’s pressure is no longer simply to find one more piece. The question reaches the frame and the prior picture: what relation was lost when this domain was rendered in this way?
findings.reason: The initialflat unstitchedpicture loses the encounteredturn/edgecontinuation; sourceworldresistance reaches the renderingframe. This does not prohibit planar diagrams with explicitquotientgluing or claim all2Drepresentations impossible.

findings.text: The pieces now acquire a different office. They become local charts. Their edges mark limits of usable description; neighbouring charts can overlap rather than merely meet along a cut. Within an overlap, the maker must be able to explain how a position described here appears there. A difference between two reports can then disclose a change of coordinates, a difference in what is being measured, or a disagreement which the available translation does not resolve. The seam becomes an operative relation.
findings.reason: Localcharts require actualoverlap/translationconditions. Differentreports may express coordinatechange, changedmeasuredobject or a dispute notresolvedbyavailabletranslation; seamalone does not manufactureinvertibility/commonmeasure.
